figure_caption: Overview. A randomized assignment on a network yields exposure features (own treatment, neighbour-treated fraction or count, optional two-hop and degree terms); a fitted outcome regression is evaluated at the observed assignment and at the all-treated and all-control corners, and the average difference is the GATE estimate. The eight-case grid varies graph family, response shape, spillover range, strength and assignment design. Error can come from sampling noise or from misspecification of the exposure mapping, which matters most at the rarely observed corners.

panels.title: Regression GATE pipeline
panels.short_caption: Regression GATE pipeline: assignment, exposure features, fitted regression, three evaluation points, averaged difference.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: a fitted outcome regression is evaluated at the observed assignment and at the all-treated and all-control corners, and the averaged difference is the GATE estimate.

NODES (IDs):
- net: a small network sketch (about 8-10 nodes, some filled = treated, some open = control) with a title label 'Randomized assignment'. Treat as data (sharp-cornered region). Draw it with plain drawio circles and lines, a few nodes only; nodes carry the symbol $$z$$ for one example node.
- feat: sharp-cornered data box 'Exposure features' containing a short stacked list of 4 chips: '$$z_i$$ own treatment', '$$f_i$$ neighbour-treated fraction', 'two-hop $$f^{(2)}_i$$ (optional)', 'degree (optional)'. Chip labels are names only. The two optional chips are drawn with a dashed outline.
- reg: rounded process box 'Outcome regression' (fitted; marked as the trained/fitted component). Small label 'fit on observed $$y$$'.
- obs: data box 'Observed assignment'.
- allt: data box 'All-treated corner' with small caption symbol '$$z=1,\ f=1$$'.
- allc: data box 'All-control corner' with small caption symbol '$$z=0,\ f=0$$'.
- pred_o, pred_t, pred_c: three small data tokens (short columns of cells) labelled '$$\hat\mu(\mathbf z)$$', '$$\hat\mu(\mathbf 1)$$', '$$\hat\mu(\mathbf 0)$$' (predicted outcomes per unit), one per evaluation point.
- diff: a minus-circle node '−' receiving pred_t (positive) and pred_c (negative); edge labels '+' and '−'.
- avg: rounded process box 'Average over units'.
- gate: result node (sharp, most prominent) '$$\widehat{\mathrm{GATE}}$$ estimate'.

EDGES (solid = forward flow):
- net → feat, label 'Exposure mapping'.
- feat → reg (solid), label 'features'. Observed outcomes $$y$$ enter reg via a short edge from net → reg routed beneath feat (solid) with label '$$y$$'.
- obs → reg, allt → reg, allc → reg: three short dashed edges (dashed = evaluation inputs, not fitting), the three boxes stacked vertically beside reg.
- reg → pred_o, reg → pred_t, reg → pred_c (solid).
- pred_t → diff (label '+'), pred_c → diff (label '−'), diff → avg, avg → gate.
- pred_o is a side reference (not entering diff); keep it visually secondary.

LAYOUT: two rows reading left to right. Top row: net → feat → reg. Below/right of reg: a vertical stack of the three evaluation boxes (obs, allt, allc) feeding the prediction tokens, then the right-hand column pred_t/pred_c → diff → avg → gate. The all-treated and all-control branches are mirror-aligned (equal size, vertically symmetric) so the subtraction reads clearly. Panel reads left to right overall.

IMPORTANCE: gate (highest), allt and allc corners and diff (high), reg and feat (medium), net, obs, pred_o (lowest).

TEXT BUDGET (exact labels only): 'Randomized assignment', 'Exposure mapping', 'Exposure features', '$$z_i$$ own treatment', '$$f_i$$ neighbour-treated fraction', 'two-hop $$f^{(2)}_i$$', 'degree', 'Outcome regression', '$$y$$', 'Observed assignment', 'All-treated corner', 'All-control corner', '$$z=1,\ f=1$$', '$$z=0,\ f=0$$', '$$\hat\mu(\mathbf z)$$', '$$\hat\mu(\mathbf 1)$$', '$$\hat\mu(\mathbf 0)$$', '+', '−', 'Average over units', '$$\widehat{\mathrm{GATE}}$$ estimate'. No raw multi-term equations; differencing is the − node and averaging is a named box.

panels.title: Corner extrapolation
panels.short_caption: Qualitative exposure-space sketch: observed data cluster mid-range, corners at 0 and 1 are extrapolated.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: observed neighbour-treated fractions concentrate mid-range, so the all-control and all-treated corners are reached only by extrapolating the fitted curve, where mapping misspecification matters most.

NODES (IDs):
- plot: [[mp:Exposure-response sketch. Horizontal axis: neighbour-treated fraction f from 0 to 1 (ticks only at 0, 0.5 and 1, labelled '0', '0.5', '1'). Vertical axis: outcome, no tick numbers. Draw a cloud of scattered observed-unit points whose horizontal density is concentrated around f=0.5 (bell-shaped) and sparse/absent near f=0 and f=1. Overlay one solid fitted line (linear mapping) running through the cloud and extended with a dashed continuation to both f=0 and f=1. Also overlay a second, differently coloured dashed curve (the true or alternative mapping, e.g. saturating S-shape) that agrees with the line mid-range but departs from it near both corners; the message is qualitative: the fits agree where data are dense and diverge at the corners. Mark the two corner points on the fitted line with filled markers. Under the axis, a small density strip or rug showing observed data mass in the middle. No numeric values, no legend with numbers; short in-plot text allowed only as listed in the text budget.]]
- corner_c: callout tag at the left end, 'All-control corner'.
- corner_t: callout tag at the right end, 'All-treated corner'.
- obs_tag: callout tag over the dense middle, 'Observed range'.
- gap_c, gap_t: two small double-headed bracket arrows (dashed) at the corners labelled 'Extrapolation' (one per corner), located near the diverging region.
- err_tag: small box under the plot 'Misspecification error' with a dashed arrow into the corner gap region.

EDGES: corner_c → left corner marker; corner_t → right corner marker; obs_tag → dense middle (thin solid leader lines, no arrowheads needed). err_tag → both extrapolation brackets (dashed).

LAYOUT: the plot placeholder fills most of the panel; callout tags sit above it aligned to their x-positions (left, centre, right); the err_tag sits under it, centred. Everything is symmetric around f=0.5.

IMPORTANCE: the two corner tags and the divergence of the curves at the corners are the focus; the observed range is secondary; err_tag is supporting.

TEXT BUDGET: 'All-control corner', 'All-treated corner', 'Observed range', 'Extrapolation', 'Misspecification error', axis labels '$$f$$' (neighbour-treated fraction) and 'Outcome', ticks '0', '0.5', '1'.

panels.title: Eight-case grid
panels.short_caption: Eight-case grid: graph family, response shape, spillover range, strength and assignment design.
panels.drawio_prompt:
Single idea: the eight simulation cases vary five factors, and each factor contrast is a single case pair.

NODES (IDs): a grid / matrix of eight case cards plus five factor column headers.
- Row of five column headers (sharp boxes) acting as the factor key: 'Graph family', 'Response shape', 'Spillover range', 'Strength', 'Assignment'.
- Eight case rows, c1 … c8 (stable IDs), each a horizontal strip with a small round index badge '1' … '8' on the left and five cells aligned under the five headers, each cell a short value chip:
  - c1: 'SBM' | 'fraction' | 'one-hop' | '$$\gamma=1.5$$' | 'Bernoulli'
  - c2: 'SBM' | 'fraction' | 'one-hop' | '$$\gamma=1.5$$' | 'cluster'
  - c3: 'BA' | 'fraction' | 'one-hop' | '$$\gamma=1.5$$' | 'Bernoulli'
  - c4: 'WS' | 'fraction' | 'one-hop' | '$$\gamma=1.5$$' | 'Bernoulli'
  - c5: 'SBM' | 'fraction' | 'one-hop' | '$$\gamma=4.5$$' | 'Bernoulli'
  - c6: 'SBM' | 'saturating' | 'one-hop' | '$$\gamma=2.5$$' | 'Bernoulli'
  - c7: 'BA' | 'count × degree' | 'one-hop' | '$$\kappa=0.15$$' | 'Bernoulli'
  - c8: 'SBM' | 'fraction + two-hop' | 'two-hop' | '$$\gamma=1.5$$' | 'Bernoulli'
  Cells whose value differs from the case-1 baseline are drawn as emphasised 'changed' chips (the single-factor contrast) while unchanged cells are muted; case 1 is the baseline row, drawn first with a small 'Baseline' tag.
- Each response-shape chip may carry a tiny glyph: a straight ramp for 'fraction', an S-curve for 'saturating', a rising-then-flattening ramp for 'count × degree', and a ramp with a second step for 'fraction + two-hop' (drawn with simple drawio lines, no plot placeholder).

EDGES: none between cases. Three thin dashed bracket links on the left margin (dashed = contrast pair) joining c1–c2 labelled 'Design', c1–c3–c4 labelled 'Graph', c1–c5 labelled 'Strength'. Keep brackets short and non-crossing, offset horizontally so they do not overlap.

LAYOUT: a tidy 9-row table-like grid (header + eight rows), five equal-width columns, aligned left-to-right in the header order above, badges in a narrow leftmost column, contrast brackets in the far-left margin. The panel is tall relative to its width; rows equally spaced.

IMPORTANCE: the changed chips (the varied factor per row) are highest; the column headers are second; baseline row and unchanged cells are lowest.

TEXT BUDGET (exact): headers 'Graph family', 'Response shape', 'Spillover range', 'Strength', 'Assignment'; badges '1'–'8'; values 'SBM', 'BA', 'WS', 'fraction', 'saturating', 'count × degree', 'fraction + two-hop', 'one-hop', 'two-hop', 'Bernoulli', 'cluster', '$$\gamma=1.5$$', '$$\gamma=4.5$$', '$$\gamma=2.5$$', '$$\kappa=0.15$$'; 'Baseline'; bracket labels 'Design', 'Graph', 'Strength'. No equations, no result numbers.
